objectives.text: The Bank Secrecy Act requires financial institutions, including broker-dealers, to develop and implement AML compliance programs, and FINRA Rule 3310 sets forth minimum standards for broker-dealers' AML compliance programs.

citations.quote: The Bank Secrecy Act, among other things, requires financial institutions, including broker-dealers, to develop and implement AML compliance programs.
FINRA Rule 3310 sets forth minimum standards for broker-dealers' AML compliance programs.

objectives.text: The AML compliance program must be reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's ongoing compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations.

citations.quote: The program has to be approved in writing by a member of senior management and be reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's ongoing compliance with the requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act and the implementing regulations promulgated thereunder.

obligations.action: develop and implement a written AML compliance program, approved in writing by a member of senior management, reasonably designed to achieve and monitor ongoing compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and implementing regulations
obligations.trigger: firm is a FINRA member subject to FINRA Rule 3310

citations.quote: It requires firms to develop and implement a written AML compliance program.

The program has to be approved in writing by a member of senior management and be reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's ongoing compliance with the requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act and the implementing regulations promulgated thereunder.

obligations.action: establish and implement policies and procedures that can be reasonably expected to detect and cause the reporting of suspicious transactions

citations.quote: establish and implement policies and procedures that can be reasonably expected to detect and cause the reporting of suspicious transactions;

obligations.action: establish and implement policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably designed to achieve compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and implementing regulations

citations.quote: establish and implement policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably designed to achieve compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and implementing regulations;

obligations.action: provide for annual (calendar-year basis) independent testing for compliance, conducted by member personnel or a qualified outside party
obligations.threshold: annual, calendar-year basis; biennial for qualifying firms
exceptions: If the firm does not execute transactions with customers or otherwise hold customer accounts or act as an introducing broker with respect to customer accounts (e.g. engages solely in proprietary trading or conducts business only with other broker-dealers), the independent testing is required every two years (on a calendar-year basis)

citations.quote: provide for annual (on a calendar-year basis) independent testing for compliance to be conducted by member personnel or by a qualified outside party.

If the firm does not execute transactions with customers or otherwise hold customer accounts or act as an introducing broker with respect to customer accounts (e.g. engages solely in proprietary trading or conducts business only with other broker-dealers), the independent testing is required every two years (on a calendar-year basis);

obligations.action: designate and identify to FINRA (by name, title, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and facsimile number) an individual or individuals responsible for implementing and monitoring the day-to-day operations and internal controls of the program

citations.quote: designate and identify to FINRA (by name, title, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and facsimile number) an individual or individuals responsible for implementing and monitoring the day-to-day operations and internal controls of the program.

obligations.action: review and, if necessary, update the information regarding a change to its AML compliance person, and verify such information
obligations.trigger: a change to the firm's AML compliance person information; and, separately, the end of each calendar year
obligations.threshold: within 30 days following the change; verification within 17 business days after the end of each calendar year

citations.quote: Each member must review and, if necessary, update the information regarding a change to its AML compliance person within 30 days following the change and verify such information within 17 business days after the end of each calendar year;

obligations.action: provide ongoing training for appropriate personnel

citations.quote: provide ongoing training for appropriate personnel; and,

obligations.action: include appropriate risk-based procedures for conducting ongoing customer due diligence, including understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships to develop a customer risk profile, and conducting ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, maintain and update customer information including beneficial ownership information for legal entity customers

citations.quote: include appropriate risk-based procedures for conducting ongoing customer due diligence, including (i) understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships for the purpose of developing a customer risk profile; and (ii) conducting ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, to maintain and update customer information, including information regarding the beneficial owners of legal entity customers.

obligations.action: be subject to (comply with) the Bank Secrecy Act, with no exceptions

citations.quote: The Bank Secrecy Act applies to all broker-dealers. There are no exceptions.

obligations.action: tailor its AML compliance program to fit its business and risks, considering factors such as size, location, business activities, the types of accounts maintained, and the types of transactions in which customers engage

citations.quote: Firms should recognize, however, that AML compliance programs can and should be tailored to fit their business and risks, considering factors such as size, location, business activities, the types of accounts they maintain, and the types of transactions in which their customers engage.

obligations.action: approve any subsequent material changes to the firm's AML program
obligations.trigger: a subsequent material change to the AML program

citations.quote: A member of senior management should approve any subsequent material changes to the firm's AML program.
Additionally, if there is a change in senior management, the AML program should be re-approved by the new management.

obligations.action: provide to FINRA the name, title, mailing address, email address, telephone number, and facsimile number of the AML compliance person

citations.quote: Members are required to provide to FINRA the name, title, mailing address, email address, telephone number, and facsimile number of the AML compliance person.

obligations.action: update designated AML compliance person contact information via Contacts in Firm Gateway promptly, and in any event no later than 30 days following any change; and review and, if necessary, update required contact information within 17 business days after the end of each calendar year
obligations.trigger: change in contact information; end of calendar year
obligations.threshold: no later than 30 days following change; 17 business days after end of each calendar year

citations.quote: FINRA Rule 4517 requires firms, via Contacts in Firm Gateway, to update designated contact information promptly, but in any event no later than 30 days following any change in the contact information.
In addition, firms must review and, if necessary, update their required contact information within 17 business days after the end of each calendar year.

interactions.description: FINRA Rule 3310 program obligations are grounded in, and required to achieve compliance with, the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations.

citations.quote: The Bank Secrecy Act, among other things, requires financial institutions, including broker-dealers, to develop and implement AML compliance programs.
FINRA Rule 3310 sets forth minimum standards for broker-dealers' AML compliance programs.

interactions.description: The obligation to review/update AML compliance person contact information under FINRA Rule 3310.02 is performed in the manner prescribed by, and cross-referenced to, FINRA Rule 4517.

citations.quote: FINRA Rule 3310.02 requires members to review and, if necessary, update the contact information for its AML compliance person in the manner prescribed by FINRA Rule 4517.

notes: Ratified scope for this item is limited to the FINRA Rule 3310 'pillars' program-establishment obligations (Q1-3) and the designation/contact-reporting obligations for the AML compliance person (Q4-5, and cross-referenced Rule 4517 duties), which are program-establishment matters. The FAQ's Customer Identification Program section (Q6-19) is treated as CDD operational-duty coordination layer and excluded from obligation extraction; the Suspicious Activity Reporting section (Q20-22) is treated as SAR operational-duty coordination layer and excluded; the OFAC section (Q23) is treated as a sanctions boundary regime and excluded. Modalities are preserved exactly as given in the text even where they vary within the same pillar list (e.g., 'requires'/'must' for the six Rule 3310 program elements vs. 'should' for senior-management (re)approval of material changes in Q3), without harmonizing the apparent inconsistency between the mandatory framing of Rule 3310 and the 'should' language used for re-approval duties. Q4's clarification that the AML compliance person need not be a registered principal is not itself a duty and was not extracted as an obligation row.
